method: Official and primary-source expansion. Each record preserves procedural status and states what the source establishes and its limitations.

records.title: Select Committee Transcribed Interviews and Depositions Collection
records.originator: U.S. House Select Committee to Investigate the January 6th Attack / Government Publishing Office
records.establishes: The official GovInfo collection preserves transcribed interviews, depositions, exhibits, court documents, hearing videos and other supporting materials released with the Select Committee record.
records.limitations: A transcript establishes what a witness said in that interview or deposition. The statement's truth, completeness and weight may require corroboration and comparison with other records.

records.title: Senate Report — Examining the U.S. Capitol Attack
records.originator: U.S. Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee and Senate Rules Committee
records.establishes: The bipartisan Senate report documented intelligence, security-planning, Capitol Police preparedness, emergency-process and National Guard response failures surrounding January 6 and issued institutional recommendations.
records.limitations: The report is a congressional oversight finding focused on security and response. It is not a criminal judgment and does not adjudicate individual guilt.

records.title: Planned in Plain Sight — Intelligence Failures Before January 6
records.originator: U.S. Senate Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs
records.establishes: The Senate investigation found that the FBI and DHS Office of Intelligence and Analysis received warnings and intelligence concerning possible violence before January 6 and identified failures in processing, assessing or disseminating some of that information.
records.limitations: This is a later congressional oversight finding. It does not establish that every warning was credible, that every official possessed the same information, or that a particular operational outcome was inevitable.

records.title: Oath Keepers Seditious-Conspiracy Indictment
records.originator: U.S. Department of Justice / U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia
records.establishes: A federal grand jury charged eleven defendants, including Oath Keepers founder Elmer Stewart Rhodes III, with seditious conspiracy and other offenses arising from alleged conduct connected to January 6.
records.limitations: An indictment contains allegations, not findings of guilt. Later pleas, verdicts, sentences, appeals, dismissals and clemency must be recorded separately.

records.title: Rhodes and Meggs Oath Keepers Seditious-Conspiracy Verdict
records.originator: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia / U.S. Department of Justice
records.establishes: A federal jury found Elmer Stewart Rhodes III and Kelly Meggs guilty of seditious conspiracy and other offenses after trial; three co-defendants were found guilty of other felony offenses.
records.limitations: The verdict establishes the adjudicated outcomes for the defendants and counts decided in that trial. It does not establish criminal liability for other people or groups.

records.title: Four Additional Oath Keepers Seditious-Conspiracy Verdicts
records.originator: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia / U.S. Department of Justice
records.establishes: A federal jury found Roberto Minuta, Joseph Hackett, David Moerschel and Edward Vallejo guilty of seditious conspiracy and other charges related to January 6.
records.limitations: These verdicts concern the defendants and charges adjudicated in that trial and should not be generalized to unrelated participants or conduct.

records.title: Proud Boys Seditious-Conspiracy Superseding Indictment
records.originator: U.S. Department of Justice / U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia
records.establishes: A federal grand jury returned a superseding indictment charging five Proud Boys members with seditious conspiracy and other offenses connected to alleged conduct before and during January 6.
records.limitations: The indictment records allegations and the procedural fact that charges were filed. It does not itself establish guilt; later trial outcomes must be distinguished from the charging document.

records.title: Proud Boys Leaders Seditious-Conspiracy Verdicts
records.originator: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia / U.S. Department of Justice
records.establishes: A federal jury found Enrique Tarrio, Ethan Nordean, Joseph Biggs and Zachary Rehl guilty of seditious conspiracy; five defendants in the trial were convicted of multiple felonies.
records.limitations: The verdicts establish the adjudicated outcomes for the defendants and counts in that case. They do not establish that every Proud Boys member or January 6 participant shared the same conduct, intent or criminal liability.

records.title: Rhodes and Meggs Sentencing Record
records.originator: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia / U.S. Department of Justice
records.establishes: Following their convictions, the court sentenced Elmer Stewart Rhodes III and Kelly Meggs, including an 18-year prison sentence for Rhodes, as part of the criminal proceedings arising from January 6.
records.limitations: A sentencing record documents the sentence imposed at that procedural stage. Later appeals, sentence changes, pardons or commutations must be recorded as later developments rather than silently replacing the historical sentencing record.

records.title: Enrique Tarrio Sentencing Record
records.originator: U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia / U.S. Department of Justice
records.establishes: Following his trial convictions, the court sentenced Enrique Tarrio to 22 years in prison for seditious conspiracy and other offenses connected to January 6.
records.limitations: This record documents the sentence imposed at that stage. Later appellate or executive actions can alter legal consequences and should be recorded separately without erasing the earlier verdict and sentence.
